checks.claim: The real orchestrator service becomes healthy before adapter proof begins.
A generic HMAC adapter is configured through a secret-reference boundary without returning the reference or key.
A GitHub HMAC adapter is configured through the same runtime-secret boundary.
A correctly signed fresh generic webhook is cryptographically accepted.
Trusted-low-risk state is established only after the signed delivery verifies.
A generic webhook with an invalid HMAC-SHA256 signature is rejected before connector ingestion.
A correctly signed but stale generic webhook is rejected by the freshness window.
Replaying an already accepted signed generic delivery reuses the original receipt and executive run.
A GitHub-style X-Hub-Signature-256 payload is verified and accepted.
A verified GitHub push is normalized into a review-gated code-update signal instead of an automatic deployment.
A GitHub webhook with an invalid X-Hub-Signature-256 value is rejected.
X-GitHub-Delivery identity is reused as the connector replay boundary.
Unsupported GitHub event classes are rejected rather than guessed into an unsafe action.
Neither runtime HMAC keys nor persisted secret references are exposed through adapter API views.
Rejected signature/freshness cases create no connector receipt; accepted unique deliveries are persisted as verified.
Verified provider deliveries route into persisted executive-agent runs through the Phase 1 core.
Phase 2 adds inbound verification only and no provider write/send mutation capability.
Evidence remains hosted synthetic webhook proof and does not claim a live provider installation, OAuth session or production ingress.
